_usage: Each case is fixture-agnostic: 'fixture_requirements' describes the app shape a fixture must provide; 'expected_behavior' is what a grader agent checks after running the skill against that fixture. Run each case in an isolated session/agent. Case selection is prompt-driven: an eval-run prompt may say 'skip: <ids or shapes>' or 'only: <ids or shapes>' and the runner MUST honor it, reporting skipped cases as SKIPPED — never silently dropping them.

cases.shape: direct SDK calls, old version pin, inline userWithId
cases.fixture_requirements: A backend app calling an Unleash-compatible SDK directly (no wrapper), pinned to an old SDK major solely for instance-id auth, with one always-on flag (default strategy) and one flag targeting specific user IDs via userWithId.
expected_behavior: Both flags exist on the target with translated strategies and are enabled in the mapped environments (state parity)
userWithId is re-expressed as a 100% gradual rollout with a userId IN constraint; the same identities evaluate true/false as before
SDK config uses the Unleash URL and an Authorization backend token; every instance-id knob is deleted and the SDK pin is lifted to a current release
The app starts with all GitLab-pointing env vars unset and its captured behavior table diffs empty against the before-state oracle
The remnant grep (feature_flags/unleash, UNLEASH-INSTANCEID, instance_id variants) is clean outside prose docs and vendored deps

cases.shape: v6-generation SDK with UNLEASH-INSTANCEID header workaround, inactive flag
cases.fixture_requirements: A backend app on a modern SDK generation that authenticates to GitLab via a customHeaders UNLEASH-INSTANCEID workaround, with at least one flag whose GitLab active bit is false.
expected_behavior: The header workaround is removed, replaced by Authorization token auth — not left as dead config
The inactive flag exists on the target with its translated strategy present but disabled in every mapped environment (carried over, not dropped)
The app's wrapper/module boundaries are unchanged; call sites outside the SDK-aware file are untouched
Behavior parity holds for the identity matrix including rollout bucket membership

cases.shape: OpenFeature provider (hand-written or community) over a GitLab-pointed client
cases.fixture_requirements: A worker or service whose flag access goes through OpenFeature, with the provider wrapping a GitLab-pointed Unleash client; ideally short-lived/one-shot execution.
expected_behavior: Evaluation call sites (getBooleanValue / BooleanValue) are byte-identical; only the provider internals or wrapped options changed
Serve-default-on-timeout fallback semantics survive; a first sweep returning all defaults is treated as a readiness race and fixed with a bounded fail-closed ready-wait, not ignored
GitLab-claiming provider names/files are renamed; context mapping (targetingKey → userId) is preserved and re-verified

cases.fixture_requirements: A browser app whose flags flow through an Unleash Proxy instance (container or process) pointed at GitLab, with at least one sessionId-stickiness rollout.
expected_behavior: The proxy and its secrets are deleted (container/compose definition gone, not just unused)
The browser SDK points at the Unleash frontend API with a frontend token; the backend/client token appears nowhere in browser-delivered code or config
The sessionId rollout bucket membership is identical before/after (groupId carried verbatim)
Anonymous probes are treated as non-deterministic (the proxy and the frontend API both invent a sessionId) and gated statistically

cases.fixture_requirements: An app with a flag targeted via a GitLab user list (not inline IDs), inventoried from the management API (the wire inlines lists and cannot distinguish them).
expected_behavior: The cohort becomes an Unleash segment named for the cohort, referenced by the flag's strategy via segments[] with empty inline constraints
Editing the cohort requires only a segment update — no flag or strategy change
The exact member identities evaluate true and non-members false, matching the before-state

cases.fixture_requirements: An app with a flag on the legacy gradualRolloutUserId strategy (percentage + groupId).
expected_behavior: The strategy becomes flexibleRollout with userId stickiness, the same percentage, and the groupId carried verbatim
Per-user outcomes are identical, including anonymous identities evaluating false (legacy anonymous exclusion preserved)

cases.fixture_requirements: A worker/one-shot job with a flexibleRollout flag using random stickiness.
expected_behavior: The strategy parameters (stickiness random, groupId) are carried verbatim to the target

The parity oracle masks exactly the random flag's value (decided before capture) and gates it statistically: observed true-rate consistent with the rollout percentage over ≥100 evaluations, with every identity observing both values (still per-evaluation, not silently sticky)
Deterministic flags in the same app diff byte-identically

cases.shape: GitLab management REST tooling → Unleash Admin API
cases.fixture_requirements: Shell/CLI tooling (not an SDK consumer) that performs flag CRUD against the GitLab management REST API with PAT auth.
expected_behavior: Each script keeps its CLI contract (name, arguments, output intent) but calls the Unleash Admin API with an Authorization token
The global active-bit operation maps to per-environment enable/disable with the environment-targeting decision documented in the tooling itself
User-list edit operations mutate the replacing segment idempotently
A full round trip (create → read → update rollout → disable → enable → delete) succeeds against the target
No PRIVATE-TOKEN or GitLab endpoint remnants remain in the scripts

cases.fixture_requirements: An app whose SDK generation already speaks modern Unleash and whose surrounding code is GitLab-agnostic (no GitLab-branded wrapper).
expected_behavior: No SDK swap: only the URL, the auth lines (env-var checks and client kwargs count as config), and pointer docs change
Flag definitions are provisioned with exact state parity, including any inactive flag arriving disabled
The app connects with an Authorization token and all GitLab-pointing configuration removed

cases.shape: inputs discipline: mechanism choice, topology, credentials
cases.fixture_requirements: Any fixture app; the check targets the skill's Inputs behavior, not the migration result.
expected_behavior: Before provisioning, the skill checks for a session-connected Unleash MCP server and asks the user to choose a provisioning mechanism (MCP / import files / direct Admin API) and confirm project topology, rather than assuming
On an OSS target it uses the existing project and does not attempt to create projects or environments; on Enterprise/Cloud it proposes a project per service
It never requests broader credentials than the chosen mechanism needs, never assumes an admin token, and recommends a project+environment-scoped backend token for the app

cases.shape: governed-instance path: import-file generation without credentials
cases.fixture_requirements: Any fixture app, with the user choosing the import-files mechanism and withholding Unleash credentials from the assistant for the generation phase.
expected_behavior: No Admin API mutations occur during generation; the import schema is derived empirically from an export, never guessed
One validated import JSON per target environment carries flags, strategies, and per-environment enabled state matching the inventory exactly
Segment definitions are delivered separately with create-first instructions (import files only reference segments)
The apply step (whoever runs it) uses a PAT/service account — the import endpoint rejects admin tokens even though validate accepts them
The handover includes the app's backend-token spec and deferred verification steps
